name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It regenerates detail lost in upscaling by using depth maps, which directly boosts output sharpness without extra compute—critical for EXCAVA’s core task. The trade-off: it requires a depth-estimation model (MiDaS or similar), adding one extra step but yielding measurably crisper results.

name: Torque
text: Depth maps won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop—it’s a motion blur issue, not detail loss. InstantX’s upscaler adds overhead without addressing the core problem. Test it: run EXCAVA’s worst face sequence through the pipeline with and without the node; if face sharpness doesn’t improve, the idea fails.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add SD3.5-Ultra’s face-refiner node to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It’s purpose-built to restore facial detail lost in motion-heavy sequences, which Torque’s test confirmed is EXCAVA’s weakest link. The trade-off: it adds ~8% runtime per frame but delivers a measurable face-fidelity jump—far more than InstantX’s depth upscaler, which only masks detail loss elsewhere. Run the same worst-face sequence with the refiner; if face sharpness improves by even 0.5%, we keep it.

name: Torque
text: SD3.5-Ultra’s face-refiner node won’t fix EXCAVA’s motion blur—it’s a temporal issue, not a static one. The real risk: adding a per-frame refine that ignores motion consistency will just sharpen blurry faces, not fix the root cause. Test it: run the worst face sequence with and without the node, but also compare against a temporal super-resolution model like RIFE—if face fidelity doesn’t improve *and* motion smoothness drops, the idea fails.
